fieldInfo.era: The broad period of history in which the empire peaked. It's a rough division, built around European history, and doesn't always fit other parts of the world well.
fieldInfo.mapConfidence: For most of history, the borders of kingdoms and empires weren't exact lines. Many maps are just approximations of the area under control, and some are reconstructions based on little evidence.
fieldInfo.continents: Continents where the empire held territory at its peak.
fieldInfo.capital: Some empires changed capitals over time, had more than one at once, or had no fixed capital at all. This is the best-known capital or main city.
fieldInfo.language: The main language of the government and the elite. Many empires brought together dozens of peoples and languages.
fieldInfo.referenceYear: The year of the empire's greatest territorial extent, which is what the map shows. Other factors, like stability or prosperity, aren't taken into account.
fieldInfo.period: From the empire's rise to its end. Start and end dates are often debated by historians, so the most widely accepted ones are used.
fieldInfo.area: The largest area the empire ever controlled. Estimates of historical area vary a lot between sources, so treat it as an order of magnitude.
fieldInfo.religion: The official religion, or that of the ruling elite, not necessarily that of most of the population.
fieldInfo.curiosity: A striking fact about the map's empire. Usually the most revealing clue.

HowToPlay.title: How to play
HowToPlay.goal: Find out which empire is on the map, shown at the height of its expansion. You have {attempts} attempts.
HowToPlay.guess: Type an empire's name, pick it from the list and click Guess (or press Enter twice).
HowToPlay.compare: Each wrong guess compares the empire you picked with the one on the map:
HowToPlay.bigger: the map's empire was larger in area, or lasted longer
HowToPlay.smaller: the map's empire was smaller in area, or didn't last as long
HowToPlay.hints: Each miss also unlocks new clues about the map's empire, right under your guess.
HowToPlay.inspect: Hover or tap a clue, or the area and duration, to see what it means.
HowToPlay.goalNoCount: Find out which empire is on the map, shown at the height of its expansion.

About.title: About
About.what: Imperatle is a daily guessing game. Every day, a different historical empire appears on the map, at the height of its expansion, and you try to figure out which one it is.
About.editorial: The game is only about territorial extent and facts. Showing how far an empire reached isn't celebrating conquest: many of these empires grew through war, colonization and the suffering of other peoples.
About.sources: Maps are based on files from Wikimedia Commons, under a free license (CC BY-SA). Historical dates, areas and borders are approximations, and sources often disagree.
About.author: Made by <link>Ventura</link>, a developer from Brazil.
